title: Flight Compartment Windshield — Installation
abstract: Installation of a flight compartment windshield pane, with the edge sealing sequence, the terminal block torque, the heating circuit continuity check and the cabin differential leak check.

sections.purpose: This task installs a windshield pane in the flight compartment, connects and proves the heating circuit, and demonstrates that the pane seals at cabin differential pressure.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the aircraft depressurised, on ground power, and with the heating circuit breakers still tagged. The edge sealant has a limited application life; do not mix it until the pane is on the lifting frame and the aperture is prepared. The heating circuit continuity check is taken before the first heating cycle, not after. A leak check at cabin differential closes the task and needs the aircraft available for pressurisation.
sections.procedure: 1. Clean the aperture land and check that the pressure seal groove is undamaged. 2. Install the silicone edging grommet LN657141K4 where the harness passes through the frame. 3. Apply the low-modulus edge sealant to the aperture land. 4. Fit the lifting frame to the pane and move the pane into the aperture from inside, with a third person guiding from outside. 5. Install the pane retention fasteners hand tight, working from the centre outwards, then torque them in the same sequence to the value in the torque table. 6. Connect the heating harness at the terminal block, taking the earth connection first, and torque the terminal bolts AES273284K7 to 4.5 Nm. WARNING: AN UNDER-TORQUED HEATING TERMINAL WILL OVERHEAT IN SERVICE. USE A TORQUE WRENCH, NOT A SPANNER. 7. Route the harness tail on the marked path and secure it with cable ties AGS173307-59. 8. Measure the heating circuit continuity terminal to terminal and confirm the reading is between 2.6 and 3.4 ohms at 20 degrees Celsius. 9. Install the pressure seal retainer and the internal trim. 10. Remove the tags and do the windshield heating operational test through a full warm-up cycle. 11. Install the console panels and the glareshield. 12. Do the leak check at cabin differential pressure.
sections.close_out: Do a visual check of the sealant fillet around the whole perimeter and remove any excess. Record the pane part number, its position, the torque values, the continuity reading and the leak check result in the aircraft technical log.

safety_precautions: Keep the heating circuit breakers tagged until step 11.
Use eye protection when the edge sealant is mixed.
Use the lifting frame; do not hand-carry the pane.

title: Flight Compartment Windshield — Installation

issue.reason: The terminal torque and the heating circuit acceptance are given per bus bar standard, the frame drilling check for the relocated terminal is added, and the continuity check becomes an insulation resistance measurement.

abstract: Installation of a flight compartment windshield pane, with the edge sealing sequence, the terminal block torque, the insulation resistance measurement and the cabin differential leak check.

sections.purpose: This task installs a windshield pane in the flight compartment, connects and proves the heating circuit, and demonstrates that the pane seals at cabin differential pressure.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the aircraft depressurised, on ground power, and with the heating circuit breakers still tagged. The edge sealant has a limited application life; do not mix it until the pane is on the lifting frame and the aperture is prepared. Establish the bus bar standard before the harness is connected: the wider bus bar of the improved pane takes 7.0 Nm at the terminal against 4.5 Nm on the delivered pane, and its heating circuit reads 1.8 to 2.4 ohms against 2.6 to 3.4 ohms. Applying the delivered figures to the improved pane leaves the terminal loose and reads the circuit as short. Both sets are in the torque table and in the acceptance table, selected on the pane standard. The insulation resistance measurement is taken before the first heating cycle, not after. A leak check at cabin differential closes the task and needs the aircraft available for pressurisation.
sections.procedure: 1. Clean the aperture land and check that the pressure seal groove is undamaged. 2. Where the improved standard is being fitted, check that the aft spar cap sub-assembly TR874797-15 is drilled for the inboard terminal position and that the upper stiffener DEL380600-05 clears the block. CAUTION: DO NOT FORCE A NEW-STANDARD PANE INTO AN UNDRILLED FRAME. 3. Install the silicone edging grommet LN657141K4 where the harness passes through the frame. 4. Apply the low-modulus edge sealant to the aperture land. 5. Fit the lifting frame to the pane and move the pane into the aperture from inside, with a third person guiding from outside. 6. Install the pane retention fasteners hand tight, working from the centre outwards, then torque them in the same sequence to the value in the torque table. 7. Connect the heating harness at the terminal block, taking the earth connection first, and torque the terminal bolts AES273284K7 to the value for the pane standard fitted. WARNING: AN UNDER-TORQUED HEATING TERMINAL WILL OVERHEAT IN SERVICE. USE A TORQUE WRENCH, NOT A SPANNER. 8. Route the harness tail on the new path and secure it with cable ties AGS173307-59. On the improved standard the terminal is 22 mm inboard and the tail is 40 mm shorter; do not stretch a tail cut for the delivered position. 9. Measure the heating circuit resistance terminal to terminal and compare against the column for the pane standard. 10. Measure the insulation resistance between each heating terminal and the airframe and record the values. 11. Install the pressure seal retainer and the internal trim. 12. Remove the tags and do the windshield heating operational test through a full warm-up cycle. 13. Install the console panels and the glareshield. 14. Do the leak check at cabin differential pressure.
sections.close_out: Do a visual check of the sealant fillet around the whole perimeter and remove any excess. Record the pane part number, its position, the pane standard, the torque values used, the heating circuit resistance, the insulation resistance readings and the leak check result in the aircraft technical log.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; the terminal torque value differs pre and post MOD-131880 and both are given

safety_precautions: Keep the heating circuit breakers tagged until step 11.
Use eye protection when the edge sealant is mixed.
Use the lifting frame; do not hand-carry the pane.
